cards.front: Recall a key point about Quality Control in Manufacturing
cards.back: Quality control (QC) ensures manufactured products meet design specifications through inspection and testing.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Quality Control in Manufacturing
cards.back: Tolerances define the permissible variation from a nominal dimension: critical dimensions have tighter tolerances.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Quality Control in Manufacturing
cards.back: Vernier calipers measure internal, external and depth dimensions to 0.02 mm resolution.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Quality Control in Manufacturing
cards.back: Micrometers measure external dimensions to 0.01 mm resolution using a precision screw thread.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Quality Control in Manufacturing
cards.back: Depth gauges measure the depth of holes, slots and recesses accurately.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Quality Control in Manufacturing
cards.back: Go/no-go gauges provide rapid pass/fail checking of critical dimensions on a production line.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Quality Control in Manufacturing
cards.back: Statistical process control (SPC) monitors production by sampling; control charts track trends and detect process drift before defects occur.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Quality Control in Manufacturing
cards.back: First Article Inspection (FAI) thoroughly checks the first production part to verify the manufacturing process is set up correctly.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Quality Control in Manufacturing
cards.back: CNC verification: test running a CNC program at reduced speed or without material to check tool paths before cutting.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Quality Control in Manufacturing
cards.back: Surface finish measurement (Ra value) quantifies the smoothness of a machined surface in micrometres.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Quality Control in Manufacturing
cards.back: Incoming material inspection checks raw materials and bought-in components against specifications before they enter production.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Quality Control in Manufacturing
cards.back: Quality assurance (QA) focuses on the processes and systems that prevent defects; QC focuses on detecting defects through inspection.

cards.front: What should you know about gcse engineering exam tips — quality control in manufacturing?
cards.back: 1. For Quality Control in Manufacturing questions, use precise design and technology terminology 2. Consider function, aesthetics, ergonomics, sustainability and cost in your answers 3. When evaluating, justify your design decisions with reference to user needs and specifications 4. Show your understanding of Quality Control in Manufacturing through both theory and practical application 5. Reference real products and manufacturing processes where relevant
